features.name: exposure_pre (OwnExposure_pre)
features.definition: own_overloaded_piece_count of the mover on the pre-move board: count of mover's non-king pieces with strictly more enemy attackers than own defenders (raw python-chess attackers counts).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (board-only, no engine)
features.leakage_notes: None. Recorded in freeze section 2.2 weaknesses: not SEE, unweighted, x-rays only as python-chess models them, whole-board count.

features.name: exposure_post (OwnExposure_post)
features.definition: Same count for the mover on board.copy().push(candidate_move). Computed per candidate move.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes as a candidate-level feature (computable for any hypothetical move before commitment, no engine)
features.leakage_notes: It is a property of a hypothetical resulting board, not of the outcome; no engine or future information. Test B result: L+Epost 0.5501 beats L+Edelta 0.5248 ('resulting state beats change language').

features.name: exposure_delta
features.definition: exposure_post - exposure_pre.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: Same as exposure_post.

features.name: L descriptors: moving_piece_type, capture_flag, captured_piece_value, promotion_piece_type, from_file, from_rank, to_file, to_rank, chebyshev_distance, manhattan_distance, gives_check
features.definition: Local move geometry and tactical surface of a candidate move; captured value uses P3 VALUES (en passant = 1).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (comparator baseline)
features.leakage_notes: L sits at chance (0.4963) within position among MultiPV-8 candidates.

features.name: material_post, piece_count_post
features.definition: Mover-relative material balance (P3 VALUES) and total piece count on the post-candidate board.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (falsifier A7 comparator)
features.leakage_notes: L+Material = 0.4955, at chance.

features.name: mobility_own_post, mobility_opp_post
features.definition: Legal-move counts for mover and opponent after the candidate move; mover's obtained by swapping turn on a copy; None if swapped position invalid.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (falsifier A8 comparator)
features.leakage_notes: Median-imputed where None.

features.name: nc_own_redundantly_defended_count_post/_delta, nc_own_max_defense_dependency_post/_delta, nc_own_king_ring_own_defenses_post/_delta
features.definition: Three pre-named negative-control relational counts from P3: own non-king pieces with >=2 defenders; max own squares defended by one own non-king piece; sum of own defender counts over the king ring.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes

features.name: ply, move_number
features.definition: 0-based ply index of the decision; board.fullmove_number.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: phase
features.definition: endgame if non_pawn_material <= 13 else opening if ply <= 20 else middlegame.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (scope selector)
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: non_pawn_material
features.definition: Sum over all pieces of PIECE_VALUE (p0 n3 b3 r5 q9 k0), both colours, pre-move board.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (tertile cuts 37.0/56.0 from derivation)
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: legal_moves
features.definition: board.legal_moves.count() on pre-move board.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (tertile cuts 29.0/36.0)
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: in_check
features.definition: board.is_check() on pre-move board, int.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (strongest scope cell 0.7574)
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: rating, band, rating_diff
features.definition: Player's rating from PGN header; B3 200-wide band label; rating - opponent_rating.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: Population-level only here; for the owner these are game-level context.

features.name: clock_ms_self, clock_ms_opp, clock_frac, clock_pressure
features.definition: clocks[ply-2]*1000 and clocks[ply-1]*1000 (ms) before the move; clock_frac = clock_ms_self/(1000*180); clock_pressure = -log(max(clock_frac,0)+0.01).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (tertile cuts 0.1066/0.5602 from derivation; Test A tertiles 0.1190/0.6100 on all rows)
features.leakage_notes: BASE_SECONDS hardcoded 180 (180+0 only).

features.name: seconds_taken, log_time
features.definition: Think time for THIS move derived from clocks; log_time = log(1 + seconds_taken).
features.admissible_for_discovery: used as a control in Test A; it is a behavioral property of the decision itself, not of the position
features.leakage_notes: Known only once the move is committed; it is decision-time behavior, not pre-move board information. Not an outcome, but not strictly pre-move.

features.name: opp_prev_think_s, own_prev_think_s
features.definition: Opponent's and own previous think times from clocks.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (opp_prev_think_s is a Test A control)
features.leakage_notes: none

features.name: wp1, edge, gap12, gap1k, n_near, n_candidates, ambiguity_entropy, is_mate_line
features.definition: From the pre-move MultiPV-8 search: wp1 = best-line win probability (mover POV); edge = |wp1-0.5|; gap12 = wp1-wp2; gap1k = wp1-wp_last; n_near = count with wp1-wp <= 0.02761; entropy of softmax((wp-wp1)/0.02761); best line is mate.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes as position-difficulty controls (engine-derived, pre-move position)
features.leakage_notes: Engine information about the pre-move position; not available to the player; MultiPV 8 at 60k nodes is 'not interchangeable with B3's [MultiPV 4]'.

features.name: standing
features.definition: winning if wp1 >= win_probability(100), losing if wp1 <= win_probability(-100), else level.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (scope selector; losing cell 0.6355)
features.leakage_notes: Engine-derived from wp1.

features.name: candidates[].wp, cand_wp, regret
features.definition: Per-candidate win probability from the MultiPV-8 pre-move search; regret = wp1 - cand_wp.
features.admissible_for_discovery: as the ranking TARGET in Test B, not as a feature
features.leakage_notes: Engine value of candidate moves; using it as a feature would be leakage. A-9: candidate set restricted to engine top 8.

features.name: wp1_after, quality_loss, post_terminal, played_is_best, played_in_candidates, played_wp, is_played
features.definition: Post-move search value (opponent POV); quality_loss = max(0, wp1 - (1 - wp1_after)); flags about the played move.
features.admissible_for_discovery: OUTCOME only
features.leakage_notes: Post-move; carries search noise (10.89% of best-move decisions exceed 0.02761).

target_definitions.name: quality_loss
target_definitions.definition: quality_loss = wp1_before - (1 - wp1_after), clipped at 0 below; wp1_after is the best line of the post-move search from the opponent's POV. win_probability(cp) = 1 / (1 + exp(-0.00368208 * cp)); mate = +/-10000 comparable cp. Centipawns never a reported unit.
target_definitions.thresholds: ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = 0.02761 ('what 30 cp costs at a level position'; common.py: win_probability_loss(15, 30)). Noise floor at that threshold 10.89%; p95 0.0429 secondary.
target_definitions.where_defined: RESEARCH_QUESTION_FREEZE.md section 3 (authority B3 FEATURE_SCHEMA.md section 9); score_natural.py; common.py

target_definitions.name: regret and pairwise ranking accuracy (Test B)
target_definitions.definition: regret(m) = wp1 - wp(m) over the MultiPV-8 list. Unit = unordered pair of candidates from the same position whose regrets differ by at least PAIR_EPSILON = 0.01. Score = share of pairs where the model orders them correctly; model ties score 0.5. Ridge alpha=1.0, median imputation, standard scaling, fit on derivation players, scored on held-out players, position-cluster bootstrap 5,000.
target_definitions.thresholds: C1 L+Epost - L >= 1.0 pp with CI lower bound > 0; C2 vs L+Material >= 1.0 pp; C3 vs L+Mobility >= 1.0 pp.
target_definitions.where_defined: RESEARCH_QUESTION_FREEZE.md section 6 and 11; analyze.py PairTable, fit_predict

target_definitions.name: Test A standardized coefficient
target_definitions.definition: Ridge (alpha 1.0) coefficient of standardized exposure_delta (or exposure_post) on standardized quality_loss with controls [ply, non_pawn_material, legal_moves, in_check, rating, rating_diff, clock_frac, clock_pressure, log_time, opp_prev_think_s, wp1, edge, gap12, n_near, ambiguity_entropy, is_mate_line]; player-cluster bootstrap. Within-player/within-game via group demeaning; leak test via within-player permutation.
target_definitions.thresholds: C4: sign held and CI excludes 0 with value controls; C5: >=7/9 bands, 3/3 phases, 3/3 clock tertiles; C6: within-player CI excludes 0.

target_definitions.name: OwnExposure decision opportunity (primary, engine-filtered)
target_definitions.definition: Both: (1) at least 2 moves in the MultiPV 8 list within REASONABLE_BAND = 0.05 win probability of the best; (2) those reasonable moves differ in exposure_post by at least 1. Declared circular: 'A player at the board cannot compute within 0.05 of best.'
target_definitions.thresholds: C7: >= 5.0% of natural decisions (F-E1: < 1.0% infeasible, 1.0-5.0% NARROW). Observed O4 34.54%.

target_definitions.name: Value-free opportunity
target_definitions.definition: At least two LEGAL moves differ in exposure_post; no engine, no value filter.
target_definitions.thresholds: Reported beside primary; observed 95.42%; gap 61 pp.

target_definitions.name: Headroom
target_definitions.definition: Among opportunities where the played move is itself in the reasonable set, the share where the played move's exposure_post > min exposure_post among reasonable candidates.

target_definitions.name: Consequence
target_definitions.definition: Among decisions where the human chose the higher-exposure reasonable candidate, share with quality_loss >= 0.02761; game-cluster bootstrap CI.
target_definitions.thresholds: C9: >= 30%. Observed 24.32% [22.95, 25.67]. MEASUREMENT_LIMITED only if CI overlaps the noise-floor rate (10.89%).

target_definitions.name: Scope-map region label
target_definitions.definition: Model-free: among within-position pairs whose exposure differs, how often the lower-exposure move has the lower regret. INSUFFICIENT if held-out pairs < 200; SUPPORTED if CI lower > 0.5 and (held_acc - 0.5) >= 0.5 * (der_acc - 0.5); REVERSED if CI upper < 0.5; else WEAK. Depth <= 2; vocabulary [band, clock_pressure, in_check, legal_moves, n_near, non_pawn_material, phase, standing].
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_REGION_PAIRS = 200; DERIVATION_SHARE = 0.60 by player.

target_definitions.name: Held-out incremental value
target_definitions.definition: quality_loss ~ controls (baseline) vs controls + exposure_delta + exposure_post (system), ridge, judged on held-out players; delta R2 and MAE reduction with player-cluster CI.
target_definitions.thresholds: 'A statistically detectable but operationally negligible gain is not sufficient.' Observed delta R2 +0.0131, MAE reduction 0.00011 (CI includes 0).

target_definitions.name: policy_consistency (owner N-of-1 endpoint, frozen, not run)
target_definitions.definition: Among the reasonable candidates available at that decision, the played move was one of those minimising OwnExposure_post. Endpoint = P(policy-consistent | eligible opportunity, post) - P(... | pre). Separate from quality_loss and opportunity_rate.
target_definitions.thresholds: Stop at 100 eligible post-exposure opportunities or 120 days; MEASUREMENT_INVALID if unscorable exclusions > 10%; overgeneralisation on non-eligible decisions = failure.

target_definitions.name: Verdict mapping
target_definitions.definition: STOP SYSTEM POLICY REJECTED: any of C1-C4 or C6 fails. STOP SYSTEM POLICY VALID, ECOLOGICALLY INFEASIBLE: C1-C6 hold but C7 < 1.0%, or C8 fails, or C9 fails. NARROW: C1-C4 hold but C5 fails, or C7 in [1.0%, 5.0%) reaching 5.0% in a named held-out-confirmed region. GO PRE-FIELD PIPELINE LICENSED: C1-C9 all hold ('It does NOT establish human transfer').
target_definitions.thresholds: As listed.

relevance_to_mission: POPULATION evidence, not owner evidence: the 45,296 decisions come from 1,333 anonymised Lichess players (blake2b hashes); erez281 is not in the corpus, and the owner's 2,209-game / ~59k-decision depth-12 corpus is a different instrument (60,000 nodes MultiPV 8 here; 'no number here may be pooled'). What transfers to the mission: (1) a fully specified, board-only, pre-move-computable candidate-level feature family (OwnExposure pre/post/delta plus 23 sibling relational counts from P3) with tested extractor and fixtures; (2) a population prior that exposure_post ranks within-position candidates +5.4 pp over geometry, strongest in check/endgame/low-material/time-pressure/losing and weakest in high-material openings, with a rating gradient (largest at 800-999); (3) the finding that the cue is a tie-breaker over an unobservable candidate set (A-11: 95.42% vs 34.54%) and that higher-exposure choices are usually cheap (24.32% >= 0.02761), which bounds how much of any owner mistake family this mechanism could explain; (4) a frozen owner-specific pre/post design (PRE_EXPOSURE_BASELINE.md: recent-300 blitz window, opportunity denominator, policy_consistency separate from quality_loss) that is the closest thing in the repository to an L4/L5 template, though unlicensed; (5) discipline reusable at L2/L3: freeze-first, player/position cluster bootstrap, D04 derivation/held-out scope search with MIN_REGION_PAIRS, within-player permutation leak control. Explicit caution for the mission: the documents treat OwnExposure as a within-position ranking regularity, NOT as a player-specific decision mechanism; nothing here shows two owner mistakes share a mechanism. Any owner-level L1/L2 claim must be built on the owner's own decisions with a pre-registered consequence definition, and cannot borrow C1-C9 passes from the population.

Does learning it change an uncued ordinary-game decision? FIELD_REQUIRED; PRE_EXPOSURE_BASELINE.md frozen; 100 eligible post-exposure opportunities or 120 days. Gate did not open, so no intervention is licensed.

Does higher exposure cost more later, at the point the opponent exploits it? PROSPECTIVELY SPECIFIED; needs a delayed-cost outcome and horizon frozen first; 'the preserved corpus cannot answer it; needs continuation searches'.

features.name: secondsTaken / thinkMs (think time)
features.definition: spent = clockTimes[ply−2] − clockTimes[ply] + incrementSeconds, clamped ≥ 0; null at ply < 2 or when TimeControl header missing; integer seconds on Lichess (`[%clk]` H:MM:SS).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes as a behavioural covariate / stratifier (the B2 study and the gradient use it); it is NOT a pre-move predictor — it is only known at move commit and is a product of the decision process.
features.admissible_for_validation: Only inside a TimedHoldout (INV-10); a static drill 'may speak about the claim but never close it' (ADR-003).
features.leakage_notes: No engine or outcome information, but confounded by reverse causation with position difficulty (§2.2); imported first moves were once written as 0 s — now null. An intervention keyed on it must be phrased as an in-game trigger ('when you notice you are past N s'), never as 'think less'.
features.where_defined: shared/pgn-clock.ts secondsSpentAt; shared/detector.ts BucketableDecision.secondsTaken; shared/blitz-features.ts thinkMs

features.name: clockMsRemaining / clockBeforeMs
features.definition: The player's own clock as they FACED the position: clockTimes[ply−2] × 1000; null at ply < 2 or missing.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes (used by `clock-under-1m` < 60,000 ms and by `time pressure` candidate).
features.admissible_for_validation: TimedHoldout only; `clock-under-1m` is not registrable while LIVE_DECISION_CARRIES_CLOCK = false.
features.leakage_notes: Clean; the after-reading is deliberately not used ('a consequence of the decision').

features.name: opponentClockBeforeMs
features.definition: Opponent's clock at the moment the player decides: clockTimes[ply−1] × 1000 (starting clock at ply 1).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Derivable but 'nothing derives them' into any scored corpus; not in the evidence row schema.
features.leakage_notes: Clean by index argument in pgn-clock.ts.

features.name: logThinkTime
features.definition: log(1 + thinkMs/1000).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes (B2 candidate `log seconds`, cuts [1,2,4,8,16] s).
features.leakage_notes: same as think time

features.name: clockRemainingFraction / time pressure (clock %)
features.definition: clockBeforeMs / timeControl.initialMs; can exceed 1 with increment, not clamped. B2 candidate: 100 × clockMsRemaining / baseClockMs, cuts 25/50/75.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes, but KILLED as a stand-alone representation (fails its null; phase ordering wearing a clock).
features.leakage_notes: Denominator must be the PGN TimeControl header, not inferred from eligible decisions (Amendment 2 defect b).

features.name: clockBalanceMs
features.definition: clockBeforeMs − opponentClockBeforeMs (positive = ahead).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Not yet computable on any scored corpus (opponent clock never derived).
features.leakage_notes: clean

features.name: clockShare
features.definition: clockBeforeMs / (clockBeforeMs + opponentClockBeforeMs); 0.5 is level.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Not yet computable on any scored corpus.
features.leakage_notes: clean

features.name: thinkFractionOfClockBefore / clockShareOfDecision
features.definition: thinkMs / clockBeforeMs (null if either missing or clock ≤ 0). Candidate cuts: fast-relative < 1/60, slow-relative > 1/15 (half / double an even 1/30 share).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Candidate only; REJECTED at these cuts on simulated worlds; never evaluated on the owner's real record.
features.leakage_notes: Point-in-time safe numerator/denominator, but the numerator is think time (known at commit). D05's own objection: 'the share a decision costs rises through a game even at a perfectly even pace, so a fixed threshold is not a fixed meaning.'

features.name: playerRelativeThinkPercentile (+ percentileSource)
features.definition: Share of a sorted reference distribution of this player's think times ≤ thinkMs (ties count as below); null without a reference. B2 'the player's own quartiles' = quartiles fitted on the derivation half only.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Only with a reference fitted on prior/derivation data and named in percentileSource.
features.admissible_for_validation: Only with a reference frozen before claim_frozen_at.
features.leakage_notes: 'a reference drawn from the same decisions being read is leakage wearing a percentile' — the one feature the repo flags as dangerous.

features.name: fast-under-45s / slow-over-2m (shipped time buckets)
features.definition: secondsTaken < 45 ; secondsTaken > 120 (requiresTime).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Frozen in hypothesis-manifest; structurally dead on blitz (0.00 pp; slow bucket n=4 on the whole record).
features.leakage_notes: A null think time belongs to neither side (`bucketable`).

features.name: clock-under-1m (shipped clock bucket)
features.definition: clockMsRemaining < 60_000 (requiresClock).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes on imports; owner rate 69.38% (n=3,752) — above the record mean.
features.admissible_for_validation: Not registrable for live play while LIVE_DECISION_CARRIES_CLOCK = false; TimedHoldout otherwise.
features.leakage_notes: Composition: late-game = more endgame.

features.name: phase
features.definition: classifyPhase(fenBefore, ply): endgame if non-pawn non-king material (both sides) ≤ 13; else opening if ply ≤ 20; else middlegame.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes (phase-opening/middlegame/endgame buckets).
features.leakage_notes: Clean; but phase explains only 0.35% of human difficulty variance (phase-difficulty.ts), and the product's 20 pp phase spread is 'almost entirely a property of the rule'.

features.name: standing
features.definition: standingFrom(evalBeforeCp): winning ≥ +100 cp, losing ≤ −100 cp, else level; eval from the mover's side at depth 12 on fenBefore.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes (standing-winning/level/losing).
features.leakage_notes: Pre-move in information terms but engine-derived: 'standing differs on 72 rows' between engines (parity study), so buckets move in both rate and population with the instrument.

features.name: book
features.definition: Position is in the opening book (isBook); excluded from eligibility.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Exclusion, not a feature (336 of 3,067 on B2; 6,213 of 59,419 on the full account).
features.leakage_notes: Book is a claim about the position and was identical (124 / 7.8%) across the engine swap.

features.name: forced (onlyLegalMove)
features.definition: Exactly one legal move; pure chess.js; excluded from eligibility.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Exclusion (11 / 325 decisions).
features.leakage_notes: Only exact-one-legal-move; 'forced-in-all-but-name' endgame positions are not excluded (flagged as the reason to distrust the 80% endgame rate).

features.name: speed / time control {initialMs, incrementMs}
features.definition: Time class from the API's `speed` field (Lichess blitz: 179 < base + 40×inc ≤ 479 s); base/increment from PGN TimeControl header.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Time buckets read blitz only (excludedForSpeed 6,879); phase/standing buckets pool all speeds. INV-8: 'speed alone is not a unit of analysis'; 3+0, 3+2, 5+0, 5+5 are four environments.
features.leakage_notes: AUDIT §1.1: base/increment are dropped by the normalizer and recovered only by re-parsing the PGN header.

features.name: ply / colour / Elo self / Elo opponent / Elo difference / increment
features.definition: Game-level covariates in the population baseline model B0 (with log(1+clockBefore), clock fraction of base, phase dummies, V_deep, |V_deep − 0.5|, log(1+ply), time-control dummies).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Population study only (never run past Gate 1); nothing owner-specific computed.
features.leakage_notes: V_deep and |V_deep − 0.5| are engine-derived at reference budget; the reference failed Gate 1.

features.name: candidateGap, V_deep(best)−V_deep(third), log(legalMoveCount), non-pawn material, in-check (baseline B1)
features.definition: Static difficulty features from fenBefore and a deep engine search; candidateGap = V_deep(best) − V_deep(second).
features.admissible_for_discovery: Population only; candidateGap descriptives: mean 0.0299, p50 0.011, p90 0.070; Spearman with RCV −0.088. Not computed for the owner.
features.leakage_notes: Engine-derived from the position only (C3 leakage scan passed 0/60 mismatches); depends on a reference budget that does not saturate.

features.name: rcv20k, rcv1k, rcvAuc, convergenceNodes, moveInstability, lastSwitchBudget, valueGain50to20k (trajectory features)
features.definition: Functions of fenBefore and a budgeted search (50…20,000 nodes, MultiPV 2) scored against the deep reference; 'None reads the human move'.
features.admissible_for_discovery: KILLED for product use (STOP-D); observation-only descriptives exist (RCV exactly 0 in 75.4%, > 0.0276 in 5.3%; moveInstability mean 2.16).
features.leakage_notes: RCV and WPL share the V_deep(best) error term → manufactured correlation; shape-only features (instability, convergence) are proposed as the non-leaky formulation (§10.3).

features.name: cpLoss / accurate (the label)
features.definition: cpLoss = centipawns lost vs the engine's line from the mover's side at depth 12 on the shipped WASM engine; accurate = winProbabilityLoss(evalBeforeCp, cpLoss) ≤ 0.027608582.
features.admissible_for_discovery: This is the outcome, not a feature.
features.leakage_notes: Post-move by definition; instrument-dependent (13.61% flips across engine builds; 11.22% across hash clearing).

features.name: PHASE_DIFFICULTY (phase-level reference)
features.definition: Median human puzzle Glicko difficulty per phase: opening 1355, endgame 1390, middlegame 1475; eta² 0.0035.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Not a per-decision feature; a lookup by phase; population statement.
features.leakage_notes: 'must never be subtracted' from the product's accuracy rate — magnitudes not commensurable.

features.name: auroc2 (metacognitive sensitivity)
features.definition: Area under the Type-2 ROC of stated confidence vs accurate, with Hanley-McNeil SE; readable if both classes ≥ 30 and |area − 0.5| ≥ 3.75 × SE.
features.admissible_for_discovery: Record-level, not decision-level; requires stated confidence — the owner has 'recorded zero live decisions', so it is empty for this account.
features.leakage_notes: Not independent of first-order performance (base-rate skew); anchor set is the repo's answer.

target_definitions.name: accurate (product rule)
target_definitions.definition: accurateDecision(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) = winProbabilityLoss(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) ≤ ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS, where ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = winProbabilityLoss(ACCURATE_CP_LOSS/2, ACCURATE_CP_LOSS) with ACCURATE_CP_LOSS = 30 (anchored at +15 cp, the worst case); winProbability is Lichess's logistic with k = 0.00368208.
target_definitions.thresholds: ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = 0.027608582058630926 (≈ 2.76 points of winning chances). Measured on the shipped Stockfish 18 Lite WASM at depth 12, Threads 1, Hash 16, hash cleared before every position.

target_definitions.name: inaccurate (population study H2 primary outcome)
target_definitions.definition: WPL(played) > ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS, where WPL(m) = V_deep(m_best) − V_deep(m), clamped at 0, V = winProbability(cp from mover's perspective); mate mapped to ±10,000 cp → V 0.9999 / 0.0001; every move scored by `go searchmoves <move> nodes N_deep` MultiPV 1.
target_definitions.thresholds: 0.027608582058630926. Secondary: WPL > 0.10; CPL > 100; CPL > 200 ('never the sole ground truth'). Exclusion E4 |deepEvalCp| > 1000 (never applied — D5); sensitivity at |cp| > 300.

target_definitions.name: Eligible decision (import reading)
target_definitions.definition: scored − forced − book; B2 additionally requires secondsTaken not null; time buckets additionally require speed == timeBucketSpeed ('blitz', the dominant class).
target_definitions.thresholds: B2: 3,067 scored − 336 book − 11 forced = 2,720 eligible (1,412 derivation / 1,308 held-out). Full account: 59,419 − 6,213 − 325 = 52,881; 6,879 excluded for speed from time buckets.

target_definitions.name: B2 separation measure and bar
target_definitions.definition: For a representation with k buckets: spread in accuracy across buckets, weighted by bucket size, fitted on the derivation half and applied unchanged to the held-out half; buckets under MIN_BUCKET merged into the nearer neighbour. Bar = 95th percentile of 1,000 random re-bucketings producing the same bucket sizes. Outcome rule §7: STOP-B2-A (nothing beats raw seconds), STOP-B2-B (beats raw but not own null), STOP-B2-C (winner differs between halves), OBSERVATION (beats both on both halves) — 'nothing in the product changes'.
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_BUCKET = 20 (chosen after §4 was frozen); nulls 1,000; permutations 200; seed 20260830; verdict OBSERVATION on 40 and 117 games.

target_definitions.name: worstBucketVerdict / account bridge separability
target_definitions.definition: Lowest measurable bucket's accuracy rate vs the runner-up; separable when separation > two standard errors of the difference; a bucket is measurable when n ≥ MIN_BUCKET_N; outcomes registered / not-separable / nothing-readable / only-one-readable / not-registrable; resolutionFactor = (bar/separation)² 'holds only if the bucket rates stay where they are'.

target_definitions.name: Calibration-gap detector thresholds (live loop)
target_definitions.definition: A bucket is reported when its gap difference (stated confidence vs outcome, inside vs outside) sits ≥ SEPARABILITY_K standard errors from the rest, with both sides ≥ MIN_BUCKET_N; a pre-named bucket uses PREREGISTERED_* thresholds.
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_BUCKET_N = 30, SEPARABILITY_K = 3.75 (six-bucket scan, shuffled-label false-positive ceiling 2%); PREREGISTERED_MIN_BUCKET_N = 20, PREREGISTERED_SEPARABILITY_K = 3.25. 'SEPARABILITY_K = 3.75 IS A MEASUREMENT OF THOSE SIX SEARCHED TOGETHER.'

target_definitions.name: Engine parity outcome rule
target_definitions.definition: Δ = largest absolute change in any measurable bucket's accuracy rate over six players; PARITY if Δ ≤ T1; INSTRUMENT-SPECIFIC if T1 < Δ ≤ T2; STOP-B1 if Δ > T2.
target_definitions.thresholds: T1 = 1.0 pp (display rounding); T2 = 13.0 pp (smallest two-SE separability bar among six players); observed Δ = 13.6 pp → STOP-B1.

target_definitions.name: Gate 1 deep-reference stability
target_definitions.definition: Position stable at N vs 2N when A′: V_2N(m_2N) − V_2N(m_N) < ε (absent from MultiPV-3 list counts unstable) and B: |V_N − V_2N| < ε; N_deep = smallest N with ≥ 95% stable at ε₁, else ε₂, else STOP-D.

target_definitions.name: H1 / H2 pass criteria (never evaluated)
target_definitions.definition: H1 (think-time DV log(1+s)): OOS ΔR² ≥ 0.01 or ≥ 2% MSE reduction, cluster-bootstrap CI excludes 0, sign stable, majority of 12 strata, survives three holdouts. H2 (inaccurate): ΔAUC ≥ 0.02 and relative log-loss improvement ≥ 1.5% for B2 − B1, CI excludes 0, Brier(B2) ≤ 1.02 × Brier(B1), ECE(B2) ≤ ECE(B1) + 0.01.
target_definitions.thresholds: as stated; floor to proceed 5,000 events and 500 players (met: 10,200 / 2,343).

target_definitions.name: D05 relative-bucket rejection rule
target_definitions.definition: Candidate rejected unless (1) false-claim rate on blitz nulls ≤ 0.02 upper 95% CI and (2) planted `clean-fast` (later `relative-fast`, thinkMs/clockBeforeMs < 1/40) validated-on-target ≥ half of `clean-middlegame` on the same run.
target_definitions.thresholds: bar 0.209 (Q8) / 0.2112 (Q9); measured 0.0000 / 0.0475; false-claim 0.0000 upper 0.0024 → REJECTED.

relevance_to_mission: Owner-specific evidence in this area is the strongest L0 signal the repository holds: a 28.8 pp monotone accuracy gradient over think time across 52,881 eligible decisions (whole record, Stockfish 18 Lite WASM depth 12), replicated at 48 / 1,240 / 2,209 games and on the separate 117-game B2 corpus, and — on the 117-game corpus — surviving a phase × standing control in all three middlegame cells while collapsing in opening and endgame. That is a cross-context pattern (L1) only in the weak sense that it spans standings inside the middlegame; the repository explicitly refuses to call it a mechanism ('separation is not causation'; reverse causation with difficulty), and think time is NOT pre-move information — it is known only at commit. The genuinely pre-move time features (clock the player faced, clock fraction, clock-under-1m) do not separate on this account (time pressure fails its null; clock-under-1m reads ABOVE the record mean and is phase composition). features.name: g (game index)
features.definition: Integer game index per decision; the cluster unit; used for split_at_game and ICC/clustered SE; also a Plant region key ('game')
features.admissible_for_discovery: Not a selector in q7 (no 'game' selector); used only for splitting and clustering
features.admissible_for_validation: Defines the game-boundary split; never a feature the judge reads
features.leakage_notes: None; one-game-only plant is inexpressible by design

features.name: ph / phase
features.definition: 0 opening (j < min(10, length//3)), 1 middlegame, 2 endgame (j >= length - min(12, max(2, length//4))); product: classifyPhase(entry_state.fen, ply) re-derived server-side
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes: selectors phase==0/1/2; shipped buckets phase-opening/middlegame/endgame
features.leakage_notes: Generator's phase depends on total game length (endgame_len uses `length`), i.e., on how long the game WILL be — a mild future dependency in the simulation only; product phase is FEN-based

features.name: st / seconds / secondsTaken
features.definition: Think time in seconds: exp(log(budget*phase_mult) + pace_here + N(0,sigma_time)), capped 900; budget = max(initial/1000/30, 1.5); phase_mult opening 0.45, middlegame 1.40, endgame 0.90; product: bounded_action.seconds_taken, nullable
features.admissible_for_discovery: Yes: selectors seconds<45.0 / seconds>=45.0; buckets fast-under-45s (<45), slow-over-2m (>120, no selector)
features.leakage_notes: Known at commit, not before deliberation starts (M0: 'at commit'). Product defect: imports once wrote seconds ?? 0 -> bucketable() now excludes null from both sides

features.name: cl / clock_ms / clockMsRemaining
features.definition: GENERATOR: clock_ms = max(0, clock_ms - seconds*1000 + increment) i.e., the reading AFTER the decision (q9 docstring says so explicitly); with clock_duplicates_time: 240000 - seconds*2000 + N(0,2000). PRODUCT: 'the clock as the player FACED it — the reading before their move' (M0 §Q2, pgn-clock.ts:106)
features.admissible_for_discovery: Selectors clock_ms<60000.0 / >=60000.0; bucket clock-under-1m (<60000); candidate ratio clockShareOfDecision = secondsTaken*1000/clockMsRemaining
features.leakage_notes: SEMANTIC MISMATCH: generator emits post-move clock, product reads pre-move clock; q9 asserts they are 'the same clockMsRemaining'. Also NULL-5 informative missingness: missing rate x2.0 if seconds<45 else x0.3

features.name: cf / confidence
features.definition: Stated confidence LEVEL 1..7 -> normaliseConfidence -> grid value; latent = clip(centre + phase_offset{0.06,-0.03,-0.04} + conf_shift[game] - 0.05*tanh((seconds-60)/60) + N(0,sigma_conf_noise), floor, ceiling) then stochastic-rounded; plant adds delta before rounding
features.admissible_for_discovery: FORBIDDEN as selector ('half the target'); shipped buckets never use it
features.leakage_notes: At commit; player-stated. DOES NOT EXIST in the mission's Lichess data

features.name: ac / accurate
features.definition: Bernoulli(p), p = base_stated - gap - drift - tilt[game]; product: accurateDecision(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) = winProbabilityLoss(eval, cpLoss) <= ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS (derived from ACCURATE_CP_LOSS=30 anchored at eval 15cp)
features.admissible_for_discovery: Never a selector; it is the outcome half of the target
features.leakage_notes: POST-MOVE (engine verdict). M0: 'Accuracy is simulated as a bit, not as an engine'

features.name: gap / decisionGap
features.definition: confidence - (accurate ? 1 : 0); per-decision calibration gap; positive = overconfident. pysubgroup NumericTarget
features.admissible_for_discovery: Target only
features.leakage_notes: Contains the post-move outcome by construction

features.name: truth_gap
features.definition: CONFIDENCE_GRID[level] - p; the realised expected gap per decision
features.admissible_for_discovery: NEVER crosses to TypeScript or to the search
features.leakage_notes: Oracle bookkeeping only

features.name: planted
features.definition: 1 if plant.region(row) was True for this decision; the one place the region is decided
features.admissible_for_discovery: NEVER a feature; used only to score Jaccard/recall and region_probe
features.leakage_notes: 'handing it truth_gap or planted would make it a memory test' (q7)

features.name: ply (j)
features.definition: Index of the decision within the game; available to Plant regions as row['ply'] (every-game-first-moves: ply<4)
features.admissible_for_discovery: NOT in frame(); no selector -> every-game-first-moves inexpressible (0.0000 on-target)
features.leakage_notes: None

features.name: clockShareOfDecision / thinkFractionOfClockBefore
features.definition: secondsTaken*1000 / clockMsRemaining; null if either missing or clock <= 0; cuts fast-relative < 1/60, slow-relative > 1/15 (EVEN_SHARE_OF_CLOCK = 1/30)
features.admissible_for_discovery: Only via bridge `candidate` flag (BLITZ_CANDIDATE_BUCKETINGS); not in q7 vocabulary
features.leakage_notes: D05: 'Point-in-time safe by construction' in the product; in the generator divides by the POST-move clock (see cl)

features.name: time control (initial_ms, increment_ms)
features.definition: Per game, drawn from spec.time_controls weights; determines budget and hence think-time distribution
features.admissible_for_discovery: Not exposed to the bridge or search (not in RecordLine)
features.leakage_notes: None

features.name: tilt[game], conf_shift[game], pace[game], imported[game], clockless[game]
features.definition: Game-level latents: N(0,sigma_tilt) clipped to 3σ (enters p); N(0,sigma_conf) (enters stated); N(0,sigma_pace) (+0.35 if imported); Bernoulli(imported_share); Bernoulli(clockless_game_rate)
features.admissible_for_discovery: Never observed; latent
features.leakage_notes: tilt is what makes clustering a live question (Moulton factor)

target_definitions.name: accurate (simulated)
target_definitions.definition: accurate = 1 if U < p where p = CONFIDENCE_GRID[base_level] - spec.gap - drift - tilt[game]; drift = gap_drift_total * game/(games-1)
target_definitions.thresholds: assert 0 < p < 1 (no clip); feasibility: floor - gap - drift - 3σ_tilt > 0 and ceiling - gap + 3σ_tilt < 1

target_definitions.name: accurateDecision (product)
target_definitions.definition: winProbabilityLoss(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) <= ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS, where ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = winProbabilityLoss(ACCURATE_CP_LOSS/2, ACCURATE_CP_LOSS)
target_definitions.thresholds: ACCURATE_CP_LOSS = 30 (anchor at eval +15cp, ~2.761 win-prob points); replaces raw >30cp rule

target_definitions.name: decisionGap / bucket gap / gapDifference
target_definitions.definition: decisionGap = confidence - (accurate?1:0); bucket gap = mean decisionGap; gapDifference = gap_inside - gap_outside on decisions bucketable() for that bucket
target_definitions.thresholds: n/a

target_definitions.name: standardError / fired (separability)
target_definitions.definition: SE = sqrt(var_in/n_in + var_out/n_out) Bessel-corrected, null if n<2 on a side or variance 0; fired = n_in>=minBucketN and n_out>=minBucketN and SE!=null and |gapDifference| >= separabilityK*SE
target_definitions.thresholds: DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS minBucketN=MIN_BUCKET_N=30, separabilityK=SEPARABILITY_K=3.75; PREREGISTERED_THRESHOLDS minBucketN=20, separabilityK=3.25; MAX_SHUFFLED_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE=0.02

target_definitions.name: validated (chain)
target_definitions.definition: selected != null AND confirmation.fired at PREREGISTERED_THRESHOLDS on validation half for the frozen key AND sign(confirmation.gapDifference) == sign(selected.gapDifference)
target_definitions.thresholds: as above

target_definitions.name: selected claim
target_definitions.definition: readVariables(detect(...)).findings[0].strongest: within a variable the level furthest from the rest in SEs; between variables, largest inside.n. VARIABLES: phase [opening,middlegame,endgame], time-taken [fast-under-45s, slow-over-2m], clock [clock-under-1m]
target_definitions.thresholds: n/a

target_definitions.name: false-claim rate (null)
target_definitions.definition: validated_claims / records on null worlds, pooled; Wilson 95% upper bound compared to FALSE_CLAIM_CEILING
target_definitions.thresholds: FALSE_CLAIM_CEILING = 0.02 (upper CI must be < 0.02 in q4, <= in q7/q8/q9)

target_definitions.name: power floor
target_definitions.definition: validated_on_target lower Wilson 95% > POWER_FLOOR on STRONG_PLANTS
target_definitions.thresholds: POWER_FLOOR = 0.95; STRONG_PLANTS = (clean-middlegame, clean-fast)

target_definitions.name: predicate_recovery / validated_on_target / mirror / wrong_proxy (Q4 scoring)
target_definitions.definition: on_target: selected == plant.expressible_as; mirror: selectedGapDifference < 0 (all plants raise the gap); wrong_proxy: selected != target and selectedGapDifference > 0
target_definitions.thresholds: n/a

target_definitions.name: on-target (Q7/Q10 search scoring)
target_definitions.definition: validated AND Jaccard(region.covers(validation), planted[validation]) >= ON_TARGET_JACCARD
target_definitions.thresholds: ON_TARGET_JACCARD = 0.60

target_definitions.name: attribution veto
target_definitions.definition: attribution(key, validation, k) splits the claimed bucket by each other bucketing; z = gapDifference/SE per split; breaks if |z| >= k; verdict unreadable if bucket-too-small or no-readable-split; bridge reports maxAbsZ over readable splits
target_definitions.thresholds: ATTRIBUTION_K = 2.5; MIN_SPLIT_N = 15; FALSE_VETO_CEILING = 0.10 (choice rule: smallest k with worst false veto <= 0.10)

target_definitions.name: selftest null pass
target_definitions.definition: |mean_gap_difference / (sd/sqrt(records))| <= MAX_Z per world x bucket, buckets with insideN<30 or outsideN<30 excluded
target_definitions.thresholds: MAX_Z = 3.5; SELFTEST_GAMES=120; SELFTEST_RECORDS=40

target_definitions.name: selftest plant pass
target_definitions.definition: |realised - delta| <= max(0.02, 0.20*|delta|) OR realised >= 0.6*delta, realised = mean(gap inside planted) - mean(gap outside), 8 records
target_definitions.thresholds: as stated

target_definitions.name: answerable (region_probe)
target_definitions.definition: unplanted*size >= MIN_BUCKET_N AND floor < unplanted, where planted = mean share planted on derivation half, inside = mean bucket inside share from bridge sides, floor = max(0, planted - inside), unplanted = 1 - planted, size = median derivation decisions
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_BUCKET_N = 30

target_definitions.name: bucket liveness
target_definitions.definition: nonempty: inside>0 and outside>0; usable: min(inside,outside) >= MIN_BUCKET_N; cleared: key in r['cleared']
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_BUCKET_N = 30

target_definitions.name: recovery bar (D05)
target_definitions.definition: candidate validated_on_target on the fast plant >= 0.5 * clean-middlegame validated_on_target
target_definitions.thresholds: Q8: bar 0.20875 (half of Q6's 0.4175); Q9: bar 0.21125 (half of this run's 0.4225)

target_definitions.name: pysubgroup quality
target_definitions.definition: StandardQFNumeric(a=0.5): size-weighted mean difference of gap; BeamSearch beam_width=20; result_set_size=1; depth in {1,2}

relevance_to_mission: HIGH for method, LOW for direct data reuse. The oracle is a simulation harness whose target is the CALIBRATION GAP (player-stated confidence minus engine accuracy bit); the mission's owner data (erez281, ~59k Lichess decisions at depth 12) carries no stated confidence, so no oracle target, world, or result number transfers directly. Its worlds contain only phase / seconds / clock / game / ply; no opening, color, material, or eval feature exists, so 'materially different chess contexts' cannot be expressed in the current vocabulary. What transfers: (1) the discipline — derive on a game-boundary half, freeze ONE region, judge on unseen games at shipped k, same-sign requirement, shuffled-label control within record, false-claim ceiling 0.02 declared before the run, on-target as set overlap (Jaccard >= 0.60) rather than name match, region_probe answerability before scoring recall; (2) the measured facts — a fixed-vocabulary pysubgroup beam search (depth 2) recovers a two-term conjunction exactly on 33.5% of records at a 0.0010 false-claim rate, while depth 1 systematically names one half of a two-term truth; the shipped six-bucket chain misattributes an inexpressible region (11-12%) and is silent >50% of the time on a 0.18 effect at 20/20 games; the decision-level SE is understated up to 38% on game-clustered buckets and cluster-robust SE fails at 20 clusters (but the mission has ~2,209 games, far past both the 20-cluster failure and the 60-validation-game veto trigger); (3) the warnings — 'do not treat similarity/correlation as mechanism' is echoed by D08's refusal to rename a claim to the region attribution found (post-hoc) and by D04's 'depth is choosing which world to be right about'. For the mission the oracle's reusable code is generate_record's construction pattern (outcome follows the pre-move statement; planted effect moves the pre-move quantity), q7.run_record's derive/freeze/judge/shuffle loop, and the Wilson/Jaccard/answerability helpers; the world model itself would need new WorldSpec fields and new selectors, each of which is 'a new multiplicity question' requiring its own null ceiling run.

utilities.name: validate_finding.py
utilities.what_it_does: Stdlib validator for a v0.2 finding JSON: enforces enums, exact field sets, evidence_refs resolution, reality floors (SUPPORTED requires observed>=required; INSUFFICIENT_REALITY requires observed<required), ALLOW requires SUPPORTED+floor, OUTCOME requires FIELD+R6 floor, ASSERT_FIELD_OUTCOME+ALLOW requires FIELD+SUPPORTED+observed>=R6, status rules for DISCRIMINATE_FIRST/BUILD_READY/FIELD_STOP, OWNER-only waiver, recursive ban on confidence keys. Usage: python scripts/validate_finding.py <finding.json>; prints 'VALID: Neta Assurance Finding v0.2' or 'INVALID: <reason>'.

features.name: position (FEN / board state before the move)
features.definition: The position presented to the player at decision time. STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM.json production_record_contents: 'Per decision, before reveal: position, move, seconds_taken, stated read, confidence with its scale and grid version, every distinct move physically placed on the board in touch order, and a randomised alternative-move probe with a denominator.'
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (board-only predicates; 'A frozen board predicate identifies positions in which a named chess condition holds, and the trigger has no parameter through which the played move could reach it' — status supported)
features.leakage_notes: Trigger predicates must not branch on the played move; STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM refuted '_threat_satisfies is the only predicate of the twelve that branches on the trigger' (RC-12 also branches). Any predicate whose negative cell is saturated (C11 'near 1') carries no information.

features.name: seconds_taken (decision time)
features.definition: Time from position presentation to commit, recorded per decision in the product record. In the historical Lichess corpus the analogous quantity is clock-derived think time (lichess_app tests/LEVELS.md notes 'Every blitz think time was a fraction of a millisecond, the schema wants an integer' defect).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes as a covariate; STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM 'plus time' observation set gave separation 0.5 (no identifying power for response-bias vs discrimination on a saturated cell)
features.admissible_for_validation: yes, if defined identically in held-out
features.leakage_notes: Known at commit time, not at decision start; it is a property of the decision process, not of the position. Does not leak engine evaluation. Whether raw seconds is the right unit is owned by docs/research/TIME_REPRESENTATION_RESULTS.md (not read).

features.name: stated read
features.definition: The player's own pre-reveal statement of what the position asks (product record field).
features.admissible_for_discovery: product-only (not present in historical Lichess games)
features.leakage_notes: Declared before engine speaks (N-3: 'confidence declared before the engine spoke'); reactivity 'untested' (STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM unresolved id 'reactivity').

features.name: confidence with its scale and grid version
features.definition: Player-declared confidence on a stated scale, with grid version recorded.
features.admissible_for_discovery: product-only; PRE_HUMAN_CEILING F2 shows per-level cells under MIN_BUCKET_N are 'too thin to read' and 'reliable is some' with 'unreadableShare'
features.leakage_notes: Pre-reveal. Note: a JSON key named 'confidence' is FORBIDDEN inside any Neta finding (validate_finding.py), so this feature must be described in text, not stored under that key in the ledger.

features.name: every distinct move physically placed on the board in touch order (considered-moves register)
features.definition: Sequence of candidate moves the player placed before committing; N-5: 'a considered-moves register exists' and reveal text 'רק מהלך אחד נרשם כנשקל'.
features.admissible_for_discovery: product-only; STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM 'plus candidate set' separation 0.5 (no power on saturated cell)
features.leakage_notes: Pre-commit; but N-5 notes 'the direct two-click path, which considers nothing' — register is empty for direct commits, so absence is not evidence of no alternatives considered.

features.name: randomised alternative-move probe (probe.assignment, 'אם לא היית עושה את זה, מה כן היית עושה?')
features.definition: Post-commit, pre-reveal interstitial asking for one alternative; probe.assignment in {probed, not-probed, ineligible} recorded on every decision; legal_moves stored beside it as covariate. N-5 measured it firing on 6 of 15 clean first decisions.
features.admissible_for_discovery: product-only, within arm only ('trial 1's reveal-to-continuation rates can be read within arm rather than across it')
features.leakage_notes: Asked AFTER commit so it cannot leak into the committed move, but it is an intervention on subsequent behavior (W8/FL-005 reactivity); N-5: removing it 'would be instrument damage'. Distinct from the DEFERred pre-decision 'which second move' probe.

features.name: 'Which second move were you considering?' (pre-decision probe — NOT built)
features.definition: Hypothetical pre-decision question that 'would distinguish candidate-generation failure from evaluation failure, but asking it may change the move search itself.'
features.admissible_for_discovery: DEFER (FL-005 encodability bias; W1-INS-001 reversal: 'Remove or defer the probe if it does not materially discriminate live hypotheses or if its reactivity changes the target behavior')
features.leakage_notes: Reactivity: a pre-event probe is itself an intervention (TF2 'MATERIAL pre-event probes require an explicit protocol tradeoff or alternative measure').

features.name: move (committed move) / engine result
features.definition: The move played; engine evaluation of it at reveal. Listed for completeness as the target side, not a feature.
features.admissible_for_discovery: as target/label only
features.leakage_notes: Post-move; the mission's 'mistake' label derives from it. STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM 'outcomeLeakControl asserts an identical table after every oracle field is stripped' is the leakage control pattern to reuse.

target_definitions.name: Claim state SUPPORTED (Neta)
target_definitions.definition: state == 'SUPPORTED' is valid only if REALITY_RANK[observed_reality] >= REALITY_RANK[required_reality]; INSUFFICIENT_REALITY only if observed < required.
target_definitions.thresholds: Ordinal R0<R1<...<R6; no numeric threshold.

target_definitions.name: Claim reality floors (typical minimums)
target_definitions.definition: element/style exists R1; isolated manipulation changes salience R2; application state transitions correctly R3; production behaves as specified R4; owner experiences the issue during real use R5; a stranger notices / users prefer / users derive value R6.
target_definitions.thresholds: As listed; 'users derive differentiated value' = 'R6 with a field design appropriate to that value claim'.

target_definitions.name: Research promotion thresholds (executable)
target_definitions.definition: TRIANGULATED+: >=2 independence_families and >=2 supporting_source_ids; ADVERSARIAL+: counterevidence_search_completed true, counterevidence_strategy text, >=1 neighboring explanation, A>=2; BOUNDED+: culture material/plausible -> >=1 represented, >=1 missing, C>=1; FIXTURE_READY+: discriminator, fixture_path, O>=3; CANDIDATE_CAPABILITY+: G>=3, A>=2, O>=3, no unresolved_material_contradiction; PROMPT_ELIGIBLE: prompt_rule_candidate, neighbor_behavior_at_risk.
target_definitions.thresholds: G 1-7, C 0-4, A 0-4, O 0-5; neighboring_explanations <=5; candidate_wording >=8 chars.

target_definitions.name: GitHub Benchmark Wave 1 minimum viable evidence
target_definitions.definition: 'the preregistered decision threshold required at least 3 clean Neta failures and only 1 was observed'.
target_definitions.thresholds: 48 adjudicated repos; 16 HOLDOUT; 14 fully surviving deltas; 8 partial; 1 clean failure; 0 promoted rules.

target_definitions.name: DQ1 minimum viable evidence
target_definitions.definition: 12 prospective real decision events; >=3 products/domains; >=3 BUILD candidates; >=3 DEFER/OWNER/FIELD candidates; >=3 discriminator-resolvable cases; >=2 Neta failures or explicit underpower evidence; >=2 surviving Neta-vs-baseline deltas. Adjudication states SUPPORTED / PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED / UNRESOLVED / REFUTED / AUTHORITY_INVALID.
target_definitions.thresholds: 'These are decision thresholds, not statistical proof.'

target_definitions.name: Field first-wave F1 minimum
target_definitions.definition: 6 prospective field cases; >=3 products/tasks; >=2 outcome families; >=2 with meaningful control; >=1 where field evidence reverses/narrows; every case has explicit authority transition into FIELD. Default '5 independent participants for formative mechanism discovery'.
target_definitions.thresholds: 'The number 5 is not a universal usability-law threshold and does not establish prevalence.'

target_definitions.name: Learning-construct evidence levels E1..E7 (chess repo, distinct from Neta R-levels)
target_definitions.definition: E1 domain semantics; E2 item/observation mapping; E3 human construct validity; E4 causal intervention; E5 delayed uncued transfer; E6 ecological transfer; E7 replication.
target_definitions.thresholds: 'Required for any product-visible learning claim: E5. Reached: E1.'

target_definitions.name: C11 criterion (noise-cell information)
target_definitions.definition: 'the prescription size on the trigger-negative cell, under the response predicate as the class's own prescription sentence states it'; fails_if 'near 1 -- the class has no noise cell and its separation is a fact about its predicate'.

relevance_to_mission: Neta supplies the mandatory shape and the permission grammar for the mission ledger; it does not supply any chess-mechanism content. For the mission to be Neta-compliant: (1) The ledger must be a contract_version '0.2' finding validated by scripts/validate_finding.py — raw owner wording preserved in raw_signal; at most 3 candidate_mechanisms, each with explains/does_not_explain/discriminator; every material claim typed OBSERVATION/MECHANISM/INTERVENTION/OUTCOME with evidence_refs, required_reality, observed_reality, resolution_authority, requested_use, permission; no key named confidence/confidence_score/certainty/probability anywhere. (2) Level mapping that the contract can express: L0/L1 (signal, cross-context pattern) = OBSERVATION claims, authority REPO (what the record actually holds), evidence type REPO_MEASUREMENT, requested_use HYPOTHESIZE/DISCRIMINATE; L2/L3 (predictive on held-out, stable under resampling) = a MECHANISM claim that may reach SUPPORTED only if observed_reality meets the floor the claim wording names, with the held-out/resampling artifacts described in evidence.description (numbers allowed as text, forbidden as confidence keys); L4 (one concrete next-game operation) = an INTERVENTION claim, authority OWNER ('whether a reversible design change is worth trying'), requested_use BUILD_REVERSIBLE/PROTOTYPE, and status BUILD_READY requires intervention, design_distinction, gate.falsifier, gate.positive_control, reversal_condition, plus must_not_change (measurement and intervention may not change silently together); L5 (prospective test frozen) = a frozen pre-field record per FIELD_OUTCOME_PROTOCOL_V1 (case_id, exact version, predicted observable outcome, smallest discriminator, success criterion, reversal criterion, reactivity risks) with the OUTCOME claim at state INSUFFICIENT_REALITY/UNRESOLVED and permission DENY or DEFER; L6 (validated by new field evidence) = OUTCOME claim SUPPORTED with observed_reality >= R6 — and the validator forces every OUTCOME claim to authority FIELD with required_reality R6 regardless of whether the person is the owner. (3) Population evidence (2013 Lichess corpus, B3, STRONGEST_PERMITTED_CLAIM) is RESEARCH-like: it 'Cannot establish that the mechanism is active in this product without local evidence', so it may inform but never close a player-specific claim (law 8, CF8 authority laundering). (4) The chess repo's own strongest permitted claim is CONSTRUCT-UNDERIDENTIFIED at E1 with 'domain: no evidence that any of this is separable from general chess strength' and 'reactivity: untested'; a mission mechanism must show it is not the response-bias/conditional-discrimination pair and must not reproduce any of the 18 forbidden sentences. open_questions: Which resolution authority owns a claim about the OWNER'S OWN recurring decision mechanism measured from the owner's own games? RAP §3 defines OWNER as taste/intent/tradeoff/waiver, REPO as what is recorded, FIELD as external people. None names 'owner behavior inferred from owner data'. The validator will force any OUTCOME-kind claim to FIELD/R6 ('third party acted').

What observed_reality level does the historical ~59k-decision engine-scored corpus occupy: R1 (static data exists) or R5 (owner used the real path with real input)? RAP gives no rule for retrospective behavioral logs; the answer determines whether an L2/L3 MECHANISM claim can ever be SUPPORTED without new games.

Where do held-out metrics, resampling stability statistics and n live in a v0.2 finding? The claim object has exactly ten fields and no numeric slots; keys named 'probability'/'confidence' are rejected at any depth.

Should the mission's mechanism candidates be registered as research claims? research-claim.schema.json requires wave 'WAVE1' and capability_family W1..W8; a player-specific mechanism fits neither without a logged amendment (research/AMENDMENTS.md rule).

Does 'one concrete next-game operation' change the measurement instrument (must_not_change / instrument friction / TF2 probe reactivity)? If the operation is a pre-move prompt or reminder, it is a MATERIAL pre-event probe under TF2 and needs an explicit protocol tradeoff.

The N-1..N-6 findings are not v0.2-valid; is rewriting them required before a new mission ledger is added to lichess_app/docs/neta/findings/, or does the mission ledger become the first 0.2-shaped file beside v0.1-shaped ones?

features.name: ply
features.definition: Index of the move; 1 = White's first move; odd = White. Player's moves only (isWhiteMove === (playerColor==='w')).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (deterministic from PGN)
features.leakage_notes: None.

features.name: phase
features.definition: classifyPhase(fenBefore, ply): endgame if non-pawn material (both sides, N3 B3 R5 Q9) <= 13; else opening if ply <= 20; else middlegame.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: Reads fenBefore since 'cycle 48'; earlier read the after-position (capture moved the move into endgame).

features.name: secondsTaken
features.definition: max(0, clockTimes[ply-2] - clockTimes[ply] + incrementSeconds); null for ply < 2 or non-finite readings. clockTimes[0] = TimeControl base seconds (NaN if header missing).
features.admissible_for_discovery: used by the frozen buckets (fast-under-45s, slow-over-2m); as a mechanism input it is a property of the decision process, not the position
features.leakage_notes: Not knowable before the move is committed (it is the duration of the decision). Berserk games inflate the first derivable think time by base/2 (no [WhiteBerserk]/[BlackBerserk] handling); 146 owner-berserk games in the 2209 corpus. Increment added back; header-derived start clock.

features.name: clockMsRemaining
features.definition: clockTimes[ply-2] * 1000 — the player's own clock as they FACED the position (after their previous move); null for ply < 2.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: For ply 2/3 reads clockTimes[0] = header base, wrong by half in berserk games. Product live path writes clockMsRemaining: null (per prereg.ts comment 'a board that writes clockMsRemaining: null on every decision'), so clock-under-1m is not collectible live.

features.name: opponentClockMsRemaining
features.definition: clockTimes[ply-1] * 1000 — opponent's clock at the moment the player began deciding; null for ply < 1.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (computed, but NOT written to decision_evidence.jsonl)
features.leakage_notes: Same berserk caveat for ply 1.

features.name: timeControl {initialMs, incrementMs}
features.definition: Parsed [TimeControl "base+inc"] header in ms; NO_TIME_CONTROL {null,null} if unparseable.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (computed on ImportedDecision, not dumped)
features.leakage_notes: None; berserk halves the true initial.

features.name: speed
features.definition: Lichess time class from API `speed` (bullet/blitz/rapid/classical/ultrabullet); null when absent.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes
features.leakage_notes: None.

features.name: standing
features.definition: standingFrom(facing) where facing = mover-relative evalScores[ply-1]: winning >= +100 cp, losing <= -100 cp, else level.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes — engine verdict on the position BEFORE the move (structurally unavailable in the live loop under R3; import-only bucket, cannot be registered)
features.leakage_notes: Engine-derived at depth 12 single-line; instrument-dependent (72/1587 rows changed standing between native and wasm engines).

features.name: forced
features.definition: new Chess(fenBefore).moves().length === 1; false if FEN unloadable.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (used as exclusion)
features.leakage_notes: None.

features.name: book
features.definition: isBook(fenBefore): FNV-1a(positionKey(fen)) in BOOK_KEYS (833 keys; positions at ply <= 30 reached by >= 0.1% of 2026-03 open-database games).
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes (used as exclusion; property of the position, not the move)
features.leakage_notes: None; false when no book loaded (bookLoaded flag).

features.name: cpLoss
features.definition: max(0, evalBefore - evalAfter) for White, max(0, evalAfter - evalBefore) for Black, evals White-relative, from two independent depth-12 single-line root searches; mate = +/-10000.
features.admissible_for_discovery: NO — TARGET-derived (post-move); feature-contract.ts: 'A TARGET may never appear in a predicate.'
features.leakage_notes: Post-move by construction.

features.name: accurate
features.definition: winProbabilityLoss(facing, cpLoss) <= ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS (≈0.02761).
features.admissible_for_discovery: NO — the target
features.leakage_notes: Post-move.

features.name: gameIndex / gameId / playerId
features.definition: Source index into games[], Lichess game id, salted sha1 of username.
features.admissible_for_discovery: identifiers only
features.leakage_notes: None.

features.name: legalMoveCount (blitz dataset / live probe only)
features.definition: board.moves().length on fenBefore.
features.admissible_for_discovery: yes, but NOT computed in the import path (only in build_blitz_research_dataset.ts DecisionEvent and live probe.legal_moves)
features.leakage_notes: None.

features.name: inCheck, nonPawnMaterial, moverIsWhite, elo, opponentElo, actualMoveSan/Uci (blitz dataset only)
features.definition: From the pre-move board and PGN headers (WhiteElo/BlackElo); actualMove is the move played.
features.admissible_for_discovery: inCheck/material/colour/elo: yes; actualMove: NO for prediction (it is the decision itself) but fine for describing it after the fact
features.leakage_notes: Not produced by the owner import pipeline; exists in the open-database blitz builder.

features.name: ECO / opening name / opening.ply / rating / ratingDiff / berserk / arenaTour / variant / status / winner
features.definition: Present in the raw API JSON and PGN tags of frozen_2209.ndjson; opening name is mapped by lichess-public.ts toGame; none reach ImportedDecision.

features.leakage_notes: winner/status/ratingDiff are post-game.

features.name: B3 engine-difficulty features (wp1, edge, gap12, gap1k, ambiguity_entropy, n_near, best_move_changes, eval_volatility, pv_instability, final_depth, nodes_to_depth10, is_mate_line, voc_*)

features.leakage_notes: Engine-search complexity, 'never described as human cognitive complexity'.

features.name: eval-analysis.ts accuracy score / classification
features.definition: 103.1668*exp(-0.04354*cpl)-3.1668 on raw cpl (cp); best<=10, excellent<=25, good<=50, inaccuracy<=100, mistake<=200, blunder>200.
features.admissible_for_discovery: NO (non-canonical target; docs/MEASUREMENTS.md: 'accuracy rate is canonical')
features.leakage_notes: Post-move; not comparable with the canonical rule.

target_definitions.name: accurate (canonical accuracy rate)
target_definitions.definition: accurateDecision(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) := winProbabilityLoss(engineEvalCp, cpLoss) <= ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS; winProbability(cp) = 1/(1+exp(-0.00368208*cp)); winProbabilityLoss(e,l) = max(0, wp(e) - wp(e-l)); engineEvalCp = mover-relative eval of the position BEFORE the move (evalScores[ply-1], negated for Black); cpLoss = max(0, signed drop in White-relative eval across the move).
target_definitions.thresholds: ACCURATE_CP_LOSS = 30; ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = winProbabilityLoss(15, 30) ≈ 0.02761 (2.76 points); equivalent cp tolerance: 30 cp at eval 0, 38 at +300, 58 at +500, 212 at +1000; mate encoded as +/-10000 (MATE_SCORE) before differencing.

target_definitions.name: cpLoss
target_definitions.definition: cpLossAt(evalScores, ply) = max(0, before - after) if ply odd (White) else max(0, after - before); before = evalScores[ply-1], after = evalScores[ply]; evalScores White-relative, from separate depth-12 MultiPV-1 root searches with hash cleared per position.
target_definitions.thresholds: None (continuous, >= 0, centipawns).

target_definitions.name: standing
target_definitions.definition: standingFrom(facing): 'winning' if facing >= CLEAR_EDGE_CP, 'losing' if facing <= -CLEAR_EDGE_CP, else 'level'.
target_definitions.thresholds: CLEAR_EDGE_CP = 100.

target_definitions.name: bucket accurateRate / measurable / separable
target_definitions.definition: accurateRate = inside.filter(accurate).length / inside.length over chosen (= !forced && !book) decisions bucketable for the bucketing; clock/time buckets restricted to the dominant speed; measurable iff n >= MIN_BUCKET_N and the bucket is fillable; worst = lowest measurable rate; separable iff runnerUp.rate - worst.rate > standardErrors * sqrt(p1(1-p1)/n1 + p2(1-p2)/n2).
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_BUCKET_N = 30; standardErrors = 2 (import bridge); fast-under-45s: secondsTaken < 45; slow-over-2m: secondsTaken > 120; clock-under-1m: clockMsRemaining < 60000; resolutionFactor = (threshold/separation)^2, RESOLUTION_FACTOR_CEILING = 50.
target_definitions.where_defined: shared/import-diagnostic.ts diagnosticFromDecisions, worstBucketVerdict; shared/detector.ts BUCKETINGS, MIN_BUCKET_N

target_definitions.name: live calibration-gap candidate (detector)
target_definitions.definition: decisionGap = confidence - (accurate ? 1 : 0); candidate iff inside.n and outside.n >= minBucketN and |gap_inside - gap_outside| >= separabilityK * sqrt(var_in/n_in + var_out/n_out) (Bessel variance; null SE if either side degenerate).
target_definitions.thresholds: DEFAULT: minBucketN 30, SEPARABILITY_K 3.75; PREREGISTERED (one named bucket): minBucketN 20, K 3.25; MAX_SHUFFLED_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE 0.02. Not applicable to imports (no confidence).

target_definitions.name: eval-analysis accuracy score (non-canonical)
target_definitions.definition: moveAccuracy(cpl) = clamp(103.1668*exp(-0.04354*cpl) - 3.1668, 0, 100), averaged per player; classifyMove bands.
target_definitions.thresholds: best <= 10 cp, excellent <= 25, good <= 50, inaccuracy <= 100, mistake <= 200, blunder > 200; evals capped at +/-1500.

target_definitions.name: counterfactual reading (live only)
target_definitions.definition: both-good / narrow / reachable / neither from isAccurate(evalCp, chosenCpLoss) x isAccurate(evalCp, alternativeCpLoss), same accuracy rule.
target_definitions.thresholds: MIN_LEGAL_MOVES_TO_ASK = 2; PROBE_PROBABILITY = 0.35.

relevance_to_mission: The import pipeline is the only owner-specific engine-scored evidence in the repo (59,419 decisions, 2209 games, SF18 Lite WASM depth 12, hash cleared, reproducible A=B=C). Its per-decision record is thin: the only pre-move features are phase (3-way), standing (3-way engine bin), secondsTaken (post-hoc duration), clockMsRemaining, opponent clock (computed, not dumped), speed, book, forced, ply. It does not retain fenBefore, the move played, legal-move count, the eval value, best move, PV, colour, ECO, rating, or any MultiPV alternative, so no cross-context mechanism (opening x colour x material x clock) can be tested from the dumped rows — and the dumped rows themselves are gitignored and absent from disk; only the report JSONs and sha256s survive. All bucket-level readings on the owner are L0/L1 at best (coarse buckets, accuracy proxy, no held-out prediction, not-separable at full corpus). The B3 Python feature extractor and shared/discovery/feature-contract.ts define the admissible pre-move vocabulary and the point-in-time leakage rule (observed_at <= commit_timestamp; TARGET never in a predicate), and scratchpad/account/frozen_2209.ndjson holds the raw API JSON (with ECO, opening.ply, ratings, clocks, berserk tags) needed to re-derive fenBefore and richer features without re-fetching. Two pipeline facts bear directly on any time-pressure mechanism: 724 time-forfeit games are excluded by admissibility, and berserk games (146 owner-berserk) inflate the first derivable think time and clock by half the base with no handling anywhere.

utilities.name: run_import_harness / runImportDiagnostic
utilities.what_it_does: Scores a set of games with the engine at depth 12 and produces the bucket readings, worst-bucket verdict and bridge outcome; drove research/harness*, harness-shipped and harness-account*.

utilities.name: BUCKETINGS (six shipped buckets)
utilities.what_it_does: fast-under-45s: secondsTaken !== null && secondsTaken < 45; slow-over-2m: secondsTaken > 120; phase-opening/middlegame/endgame: d.phase === …; clock-under-1m: clockMsRemaining !== null && < 60_000. Plus separability test (SEPARABILITY_K=3.75, MIN_BUCKET_N=30).

utilities.name: IMPORT_BUCKETINGS (standing) and worstBucketVerdict
utilities.what_it_does: standing-winning / standing-level / standing-losing from the engine eval of the position faced (±1 pawn boundary); min-of-nine vs runner-up at two standard errors; cannot produce a claim.

utilities.name: classifyPhase / nonPawnMaterial
utilities.what_it_does: ENDGAME_MATERIAL_THRESHOLD = 13, OPENING_MAX_PLY = 20; phase from FEN before the move and ply.

utilities.name: win-probability
utilities.what_it_does: winProbability(eval) with k = 0.00368208; winProbabilityLoss(eval, cpLoss); ACCURATE_WIN_PROBABILITY_LOSS = 2.76.
